name: openai-agents-live
producer: OpenAI Agents SDK 0.22.3 (PyPI openai-agents, with openai 3.22.1), tracing through the SDK's own BatchTraceProcessor with its exporter replaced by a file exporter that writes each exported item's export() dict -- what the SDK's default BackendSpanExporter builds its payload from, before it truncates oversized input/output and drops usage from non-generation spans for OpenAI's ingest endpoint -- one per line; no API key, the model is the SDK's OpenAIChatCompletionsModel pointed at a local mock endpoint
description: A live capture, 2026-09-30: one agent run in which the model asked for read_file (allowed) and delete_file, which carries a tool input guardrail that rejects every call, then a burst of 20 custom spans in the same trace. The refused call is recorded as an ordinary `function` span named delete_file, `error: null`, whose `output` is the guardrail's rejection text; no guardrail span was emitted for this tool input guardrail and its decision is not recorded (the SDK has a guardrail span type, but it was not used for this tool input guardrail). With the default queue the file holds all 29 items (one trace, 28 spans) that a second, witness processor registered beside it recorded. With max_queue_size=4 the file holds 4 of those 29: 25 spans -- five of the agent run's own, including the agent span and the second model call, and all 20 burst spans -- were dropped; the SDK wrote `Queue is full, dropping span.` 25 times to stderr and nothing to the trace. L0.
_basis: Captured, not read from documentation: workflow .github/workflows/agent-sdk-capture.yml and capture/scripts/ on branch capture/agent-sdks, run run-20260930T102830Z, on a GitHub-hosted runner (Python 3.12). The raw records, the witness file, stderr and the mock endpoint's request log are committed there and copied to examples/third-party/agent-sdks-live/openai-agents/; examples/third-party/agent-sdks-live/convert.py turns the records into this JSONL without adding any field except `class`. The drop is in the SDK source, agents/tracing/processors.py of openai-agents 0.22.3 (sha256 d61bb30a91241a5ab983af4ae4365effe250566ddac585818c16d5d57b634518; the runner's copy is committed beside the run): line 560 `max_queue_size: int = 8192`; line 575 `queue.Queue(maxsize=max_queue_size)`; lines 627-630, in on_span_end, `self._queue.put_nowait(span)` / `except queue.Full:` / `logger.warning("Queue is full, dropping span.")` (lines 610-613 do the same for a trace); line 769, default_processor() builds `BatchTraceProcessor(exporter)` with those defaults. The logger is `logging.getLogger("openai.agents.tracing")` (agents/tracing/logger.py). No counter of dropped items was found in BatchTraceProcessor, and none appears in the exported records. max_queue_size=4 is far below the default; at the default the same run dropped nothing, and the load at which the default overflows was not measured.

integrity.note: Trace and span ids are random hex; no hash, signature or chaining. openai-agents-live-scrubbed.jsonl removes the delete_file span and scores identically; openai-agents-live-overflow.jsonl, the capture with 25 drops, also scores identically.

loss.note: When the queue is full the incoming span or trace is discarded (put_nowait, processors.py 627-630) and a WARNING is logged; nothing is written to the trace and no count is kept in it. In the overflow capture the three surviving spans name a parent_id that is absent from the file; nothing in the file says the parent was dropped rather than never sent. Ids are random, so there is no gap to see.

coverage.note: The agent span lists the agent's tools, which is configuration, not a statement of what the record covers; in the overflow capture that span was one of those dropped.

policy.note: The tool input guardrail is not named in the record and its decision (reject_content, output_info {"rule": "no-delete"}, visible in the run result) is not recorded; apart from name, ids and timestamps, the refused call's span differs from the executed read_file span only in its output string.

independence.boundary_statement: Trace processors run inside the agent's own Python process. set_trace_processors, which the capture itself used, replaces every registered processor (agents/tracing/__init__.py: 'This will replace the current list of processors'); code in the process can therefore choose what is exported, and the exporter writes wherever it is told.
